subject: Violin Plot Trimming and Bandwidth Cause Unexpected Changes

messages.author: 7b36a5521b8eb4d4
messages.subject: Violin Plot Trimming and Bandwidth Cause Unexpected Changes
parts:
The trim argument's description implies that it only changes the end positions of the density. However, for some data, it also draws a vertical line through the entire density area. This is undesirable.

Using the plotData data frame,

library(ggplot2)
plot <- ggplot(plotData, aes(x = analysis, y = overlap)) + geom_violin() + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
plot     # No vertical bar.
plot <- ggplot(plotData, aes(x = analysis, y = overlap)) + geom_violin(trim = FALSE) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
plot     # Vertical bar for all three violins.

The bandwidth adjustment parameter causes more strangeness, with a wedge placed in the middle of the violin.

plot <- ggplot(plotData, aes(x = analysis, y = overlap)) + geom_violin(trim = FALSE, adjust = 2) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
plot    # Strange wedge.
